comparator.name: Bachelor Mechanical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–2027 Mechanical Engineering/Marine Technology OER curriculum table (PDF page index 25), rechecked on 15 October 2026, establishes the 25 stored components and their 180-EC total. Each of Years 1 and 2 contains ten 6-EC units. Year 1 separately credits Design Projects 1, 2, 3A and 3B; the public page groups 3A and 3B as one third design project. Year 2 contains four project units: Advanced Engineering Design, Process Engineering and Thermodynamics, Robotics, and Materials Science. Year 3 preserves the approved 30-EC minor and requires Systems and Control Engineering 6 EC, Integrated Mechanical Systems 6 EC, Engineer and Society 4 EC and the Bachelor Final Project 14 EC. Mathematics/mechanics subparts remain within their credited parent units. No named route requires selection. The previously verified component identities, weights and neutral route decision are preserved.
components: Genuine first-semester minor space preserved from the official curriculum.

core: Mechanical science, materials, thermal and fluid processes, manufacturing, integrated engineering design and experimental projects
Calculus, linear algebra, differential equations, probability, numerical methods, signals and mathematical system models
Robotics, motion planning, automated systems, computational control and reliable machine behaviour
Product design, modelling, prototyping, experimental evaluation and lifecycle-sensitive development
adjacent: Energy-efficient technologies, renewable energy assessment, repair/reuse, circular resources and sustainable technical systems
questions: How can mathematical models and computational methods support automated motion, perception and technical decisions?
How can technical systems reduce energy demand and material use throughout product lifecycles?

alternatives.label: Mathematical modelling & autonomous technology
alternatives.labelReason: Mathematics, programming, algorithms, data analysis, machine learning and robotics dominate the completed curriculum. Product development, lifecycle analysis and renewable-energy assessment are specific supporting applications; the title does not imply a complete Mechanical Engineering degree.
alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical models, signals, numerical analysis, programming, algorithms, perception, robotics and autonomous decision methods. Product development, lifecycle assessment and renewable-system analysis provide a bounded design-and-sustainability strand alongside the computational core.
progression: Programming precedes dependent computing; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks; Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and Renewable System Design. Data Science and Linear Algebra precede Machine Learning and advanced neural work. All exact term availability and formal prerequisites were checked.

alternatives.label: Quantitative models, renewable energy & circular resources
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines mathematical and data methods with environmental systems, geothermal/resource investigation, circular recovery and renewable-system assessment. These are specific sustainable-technology studies, without claims to mechanical thermodynamics, structural materials or manufacturing engineering.
alternatives.concept: Study sustainable technical systems through quantitative modelling, Earth-system processes, geothermal and material resources, lifecycle analysis, resource recovery and renewable-energy assessment. Programming, mathematical methods and scientific data analysis support this energy-and-resources direction.
progression: Dynamic Earth precedes soils, biogeochemistry and resource work. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II and all dependent environmental courses. Mathematical Methods and Linear Algebra precede advanced mathematical and neural-network work. All exact term availability and formal prerequisites were checked.
alternatives.distinctness: Seven courses (52.5 EC) differ in each direction. Logic, networks, algorithms, optimisation, robotics, AI decisions and reinforcement learning give way to Dynamic Earth, Earth-system tools, soils/aquifers, climate science, environmental biogeochemistry, resource recovery and advanced resource research. This shifts the substantive focus from autonomous computation to renewable technology and circular resource systems.

candidates.label: Energy-efficient technologies and circular resource systems

selection.assessment: The strongest complete related response develops mathematical, computational, robotic and product-development methods; it does not reproduce the mechanical-science core. The independently evidenced energy-efficiency and circularity direction supports a second curriculum with seven substantively different courses. Structural materials/manufacturing was then rejected because the workbook lacks solid mechanics, mechanics of materials, engineering-materials testing and manufacturing-process progression; introductory materials in Sustainability Essentials II and one Consumer Product Design project cannot supply that spine. Thermal/fluid engineering was assessed separately: renewable-energy assessment and soils/aquifer investigation do not supply thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat-transfer theory or thermal-system laboratories. Neither direction supports a third complete coherent 24-course programme.

blocks: Both teach calculus for quantitative technical problems; UCR is a general mathematics gateway.
Both directly teach linear algebra, matrices and linear transformations.
Both extend calculus and differential-equation methods; UCR is not embedded in mechanical engineering.
Probability and statistics are a major named part of the integrated comparator unit; UCR does not reproduce its full numerical-mathematics scope.
Both directly study signals and linear-system response, including mathematical transforms; the engineering context differs.
Robotic kinematics and motion planning are substantive shared topics; UCR does not reproduce the integrated engineering hardware project.
Both undertake product-design and prototype work; UCR concerns a consumer product and does not reproduce the cumulative mechanical design projects.

notes.text: These UCR programmes offer related mathematical, autonomous-system, product-development and sustainable-resource studies. They do not reproduce statics, mechanics of materials, mechanical dynamics, thermodynamics, fluid flow and heat transfer, engineering materials/manufacturing, mechanical laboratories, integrated control hardware or the cumulative mechanical-design and final-project sequence.

Selected course content, profiles, formal prerequisites and exact planned terms were checked against the current GitHub data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, SHA-256 7bf6c2ae9de0837086ec741c27bd94ed7e85dff2d25bde619ecd50cc4d685879. All 151 rows were inspected for possible coherent directions; courses without planned availability were excluded.
